source.title: On Global Hyperbolicity of Spacetimes: Topology Meets Functional Analysis

accepted.question_text: Let (A, ≺) be a globally hyperbolic partially ordered set, meaning in particular that it carries an interval topology and that its closed intervals [a, b] = {x : a ≼ x ≼ b} are compact in that topology. Does compactness of these intervals by itself force (A, ≺) to be bicontinuous? More specifically, is there an order-theoretic analogue of the spacetime result that compact causal diamonds in the Alexandrov topology imply strong causality in non-compact spacetimes of dimension strictly greater than 2? If such an analogue exists, what should play the role of the condition “dimension strictly greater than 2” for globally hyperbolic posets, and is it possible that no dimension-type restriction is needed in the poset setting even though it is needed for spacetimes?

evidence.quote: Question 1: Consider a globally hyperbolic poset (A, ≺). Does the compactness of the intervals [a, b], under the interval topology, imply the bicontinuity of (A, ≺), in a similar fashion that the compactness in the closed diamonds in a spacetime M, under the Alexandrov topology TA, implies the (strong) causality of M (for dimensions strictly greater than 2)?

The only problem, towards [16], of considering a globally hyperbolic poset, is that we are left only with an order-theoretic structure; what would be, if there is such, the equivalent condition in [16] of “dimension strictly greater than 2”? Is there a possibility that the condition on the dimension applies only to
globally hyperbolic spacetimes, while the proposed conjecture holds in globally hyperbolic posets without any restriction?

accepted.question_text: Is there a spacetime topology, different from the usual manifold topology, that is both mathematically fruitful and physically meaningful but has not yet been considered? If so, what criteria should be used to choose such a topology, and in particular how should the chosen topology interact with or reflect a foliation of spacetime?

evidence.quote: Question 2: As we have seen in this section, there are many different candidates for spacetime topologies is, other than the manifold one. Is there a fruitful4 and physically meaningful spacetime topology that was not considered so far? What are the criteria for choosing it? For example, how should such a topology be related to the foliation of a spacetime?

These questions certainly need a more systematic work, because even if they can touch important problems (for example the singularity problem in relativity theory as well as Penrose’s cosmic censorship conjecture), they seem underestimated until now.

accepted.question_text: Given the equivalence between the category of globally hyperbolic posets and the category of interval domains, can the topology of a spacetime be reconstructed in a technically rigorous way from the topology of an interval domain? Moreover, since topologies such as the Zeeman fine topology, Göbel’s generalization, and the Hawking–King–McCarthy topology are not metrizable, does that non-metrizability help identify an appropriate spacetime topology other than the manifold topology when interval domains are taken as the underlying order-theoretic model?
accepted.context_brief: Reconstructing spacetime topology from interval domains

evidence.quote: Question 3: In the light of Theorem 3.8, we ask whether the topology of a spacetime can be reconstructed, in some technical and rigorous way, from the topology of an interval domain.

The spacetime topologies that we have mentioned in this section, like for example the Zeeman fine topology or its generalization by Göbel, or the one by Hawking-King-McCarthy are not metrizable; does this give us any insight on the appropriate candidate for a spacetime topology (other than the manifold topology), given that interval domains are order-theoretic objects?

accepted.question_text: For a general non-stationary globally hyperbolic spacetime with metric of the form g = -N^2(t, x) dt^2 + g_{Σ,ij}(t, x) dxi dxj, what precise connection, if any, holds between global hyperbolicity of the Lorentzian manifold and essential self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian appearing in the Klein–Gordon equation? Equivalently, beyond the static, warped-product, and uniformly bounded sliced-space cases discussed in the paper, when does global hyperbolicity force geodesic completeness of the conformally transformed spatial slices (Σ_t, g̃_{Σ_t}), which is the ingredient used to prove essential self-adjointness?
accepted.context_brief: Non-stationary case: global hyperbolicity versus self-adjointness

evidence.quote: In the case of non-stationary spacetimes, however, the connection between global hyperbolicity and self-adjointness of the spatial Laplacian is still unclear.
Our strategical reason for the conformal transformation is our interest in the connection of global hyperbolicity and the geodesic completeness of the Riemannian manifold (Σt, g˜Σt) for all t ∈ R.

In general however, i.e. apart from the three classes discussed above, there is no direct connection between geodesic completeness of the hypersurfaces and global hyperbolicity the Lorentzian manifold5.
